text: Why was the 2.4 GHz ISM band available for unlicensed use in 1985?
choices: It was reserved for future expansion
It was regarded as spectral wasteland — set aside for equipment generating radio energy as a by-product, notably microwave ovens
It had the best propagation characteristics
It was donated by a manufacturer
explanation: Nobody with a licence wanted it. Michael Marcus has described the decision as making rubbish land available to anyone willing to build on it, and what was built on it was Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Zigbee.
